tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Performing a Character from a Script

questions.question: Explain what actioning is and how it helps an actor deliver lines more effectively.
questions.correctAnswer: Actioning assigns a transitive verb to each line (I CONVINCE, I INTIMIDATE, I PLEAD). It gives every line a purpose, prevents flat delivery, and ensures the actor is always DOING something to the other character, not just saying words.

questions.question: Describe the vocal and physical skills you would use to perform a character experiencing a crisis of confidence.
questions.correctAnswer: Vocal: quieter volume, hesitant pace, rising pitch on questions, long pauses before responses. Physical: closed posture, avoiding eye contact, fidgeting hands, retreating spatially. Each choice justified by the character's internal state.

questions.question: How can an actor maintain truthfulness in performance without simply 'acting' emotions?
questions.correctAnswer: Truthfulness comes from understanding what the character WANTS and pursuing it honestly, not from pretending to feel emotions. If you focus on the objective and the action, the emotion follows naturally. Stanislavski: play the action, not the feeling.
